paragraphs: Friend, let's talk about what just happened to David. He wanted to march into that battle, and he got sent home. David asks, "But what have I done?" (1 Samuel 29:8), and I think that question stings because he showed up and did everything right. Achish even says David has been upright and "as pleasing in my sight as an angel of God" (1 Samuel 29:6, 9), and it still wasn't enough to keep David in that line.

So here's the lesson, baker. A closed door doesn't always mean you did something wrong. Sometimes the door shuts and nobody hands you a reason that makes you feel better. I've sat in the back of a junk drawer for years wondering what I did to land there, and I never found a reason I liked. The text says David was sent back by the Philistine commanders (1 Samuel 29:4), and that's all it tells us here.

But watch where David ends up: walking away from a fight against Israel. I'm not going to tell you what the text doesn't say about why. What I can tell you is that the story isn't over, and neither is yours. When you get sent home early, keep your oven warm and keep walking, because this story is far from finished (1 Samuel 29:11).
